avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Nizatidine increases gastric pH, reducing iron absorption
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2 hours; monitor for anemia

avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Reduced gastric acidity decreases calcium bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Take calcium at least 2 hours before or after nizatidine

avoid_supplements.name: B12 (Cyanocobalamin)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Reduced gastric acid impairs intrinsic factor-dependent B12 absorption
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor B12 levels with long-term use; consider sublingual or parenteral B12

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Elevated gastric pH may modestly reduce magnesium absorption
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for adequate magnesium status; space dosing when possible

caution_supplements.name: Antacids containing aluminum or magnesium
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential additive effects and altered absorption kinetics
caution_supplements.action: Separate administration by 2 hours if concurrent use necessary

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods/beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Caffeine may stimulate gastric acid production, potentially reducing nizatidine efficacy
caution_foods.action: Limit coffee, tea, and cola; monitor symptom control

caution_foods.name: Spicy or acidic foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May irritate gastric mucosa and reduce therapeutic benefit
caution_foods.action: Counsel to avoid if symptoms worsen; individualize based on tolerance

monitoring_notes: Monitor vitamin B12 and magnesium levels during chronic nizatidine therapy, particularly in elderly patients or those on prolonged treatment. Advise spacing of supplements from nizatidine dosing to optimize absorption.
